Rule Contents: SY-SUBRC must be checked only if the EXCEPTION statement is used when calling a function module.
The return code SY-SUBRC must be tested immediately after the statement being checked.
All exceptions raised using the RAISE statement must be declared in the function module interface.
All exceptions declared in the function module interface must be used at least once.
Authorization checks must be implemented using authorization objects and the AUTHORITY-CHECK statement.
Standard authorization objects should be used whenever possible.
Authorization checks must not be implemented by checking user role assignments, as role checks are not robust enough.
The profiles SAP_ALL and SAP_NEW must not be used.
Authorization object S_TABU_DIS must be used only for Z* authorization groups in business roles.
No change of the current user (SY-UNAME) must be done at runtime.
When message logs are required, they must be handled using standard SAP logging functions (transaction SLG1).
Sensitive data must not be included in log messages.
SAP password hash data must not be made public, as it contains sensitive personal information.
SELECT * must not be used on sensitive tables or views (USR02, USH02, USRPWDHISTORY, USH02_ARC_TMP, VUSER001, VPWD_USR02); fields must be selected individually.
Sensitive data must not be included in any MESSAGE (success, error, warning, or information) presented to the end user.
MESSAGE statements (message class and number) must not contain any sensitive data.
Change logs should not be activated on application tables due to the large volume of generated data.
The only acceptable exception for using cl_http_client=>create_by_url is when the API URL is dynamic (e.g. AWS endpoints for large files).
REST or OData APIs should be used as the preferred solution compared to SOAP web services.
cl_http_client=>create_by_url must not be used; cl_http_client=>create_by_destination must be used instead.
The use of ABAP IMPORT/EXPORT commands to/from memory should be limited and justified only after a detailed requirement analysis; alternate solutions should also be studied.
Shared memory objects created using transaction SHMA must not be used.
Sensitive data must not be stored in a Parameter ID; Parameter IDs use GET/SET commands to access data in global memory.
The Shared Memory Enabled flag must not be set for custom classes.
Binary files (jar, exe) must not be uploaded inside the content server.
